'''''Brahea armata''''', commonly known as the '''blue fan palm''', '''blue hesper palm''' or '''Mexican blue palm'''<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pérez-Alquicira |first=Jessica |last2=V. Wehncke |first2=Elisabet |last3=A. García-Loza |first3=Gustavo |last4=C. Carstens |first4=Bryan |last5=A. Domínguez |first5=César |last6=Pérez-Ishiwara |first6=Rubén |last7=E. Molina-Freaner |first7=Francisco |last8=del Pilar Zamora-Tavare |first8=María |last9=Rico |first9=Yessica |last10=Cabrera-Toledo |first10=Dánae |last11=Vargas-Ponce |first11=Ofelia |last12=Rodríguez |first12=Aarón |last13=Ezcurra |first13=Exequiel |date=11 March 2023 |title=Geographic isolation and long-distance gene flow influence the genetic structure of the blue fan palm Brahea armata (Arecaceae) |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10265-023-01445-9 |journal=Springer Nature}}</ref>, is a [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Arecaceae]], native to [[Baja California]], [[Mexico]]. Outside its natural range, it is often planted as an [[Ornamental plant|ornamental]], valued for its striking grey-blue fronds.

== Description ==
The blue fan palm grows to a height of {{convert|15|m}},<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zimmerpalmen.net/blaue-hesperidenpalme/| title =Blaue Hesperidenpalme (Brahea Armata)| date =28 October 2020|language=de}}</ref>  with a stout trunk. Its distinctly bluish leaves are {{convert|1|-|2|m}} wide, with {{convert|1|m|adj=on}} long [[petiole (botany)|petiole]]s. The leaves are persistent in nature, forming a shag around the trunk; in cultivation they are typically burned or cut off. The [[inflorescence]]s extend out beyond the crown, reaching {{convert|5|m}} in length. The flowers themselves are small, appearing in February and March, while the fruits are {{convert|18|-|24|mm}} in length, brown and with a generally ovoid to globose shape.

== Distribution and habitat ==
[[File:Brahea armata 55075626.jpg|thumb|In habitat, Baja California, Mexico]]
[[File:Brahea armata 6193266.jpg|left|thumb|Plants growing in habitat]]
This species is [[Endemism|endemic]] to the [[Mexico|Mexican]] state of [[Baja California]], distributed from just 8 miles south of the [[Mexico–United States border|international border]] near the [[Jacumba Mountains]], to the [[Baja California desert|central desert]] and [[Isla Ángel de la Guarda|Isla Angel de la Guarda]]. Plants growing in the [[Sierra de San Francisco]] in [[Baja California Sur]] may be of a different species.<ref name="rebman">{{Cite journal|last1=Rebman|first1=J. P.|last2=Gibson|first2=J.|last3=Rich|first3=K.|date=2016|title=Annotated checklist of the vascular plants of Baja California, Mexico|url=http://sdplantatlas.org/pdffiles/BajaChecklist2016.pdf|journal=San Diego Society of Natural History|volume=45|pages=274}}</ref> It is locally common in [[Arroyo (watercourse)|arroyo]]s and canyon bottoms, and has been observed growing in rock crevices at higher elevations. It is sometimes found with ''[[Washingtonia filifera|Washingtonia filifera var. filifera]]'' or ''[[Washingtonia filifera var. robusta]]''.

== Ecology ==

== Uses ==
''Brahea armata'' has an attractive appearance, especially when young, and is commonly available at nurseries in the American southwest and in warm temperate locations elsewhere. In the [[United Kingdom|UK]] it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/19713/i-Brahea-armata-i/Details| title = Brahea armata | work = RHS Plantfinder |accessdate=12 January 2018}}</ref> 
It is drought tolerant (although occasional deep irrigation is recommended), can handle both partial shade and full sun, and temperatures down to {{convert|-10|C|abbr=on}}. It is found under a variety of names, including "Mexican blue palm", "blue hesper palm", "big blue hesper palm", "blue fan palm", "sweet brahea", and "palma blanca".
